title: Building jobs grow by change order; the City still does not score how its builders perform

beats.text: When a San Francisco building job runs over, is it the builder? Or the City?
In May 2026, the Board’s Budget and Legislative Analyst reported.

visual.label: Budget and Legislative Analyst
visual.sub: 297 construction contracts, five departments, July 2021 to June 2024

beats.text: It totaled the change orders on 297 City building contracts.

visual.label: Budget and Legislative Analyst
visual.sub: 297 construction contracts, five departments, July 2021 to June 2024

beats.text: 186.8 million dollars, in three years.

visual.label: added by approved change orders, July 2021 to June 2024
visual.sub: 8% on top of the first contract value

beats.text: A change order adds work or money to a signed contract. These are official findings, by the City’s own auditors.

visual.label: A change order
visual.sub: more work or money on a signed contract

beats.text: They also found the law requires a database scoring builders.

visual.line: a contractor evaluation database that the law requires and departments do not use

beats.text: Departments don’t use it. So no one can say who runs over.

visual.line: a contractor evaluation database that the law requires and departments do not use

beats.text: A Civil Grand Jury asked that departments start entering those scores by the end of 2022.

visual.line: We recommend that by 12/31/2022, the Mayor require all Chapter 6 departments to begin submitting evaluations into the database.

beats.text: The Controller’s 2025 status table gives the answer: it will not be implemented.
Take Crystal Springs/San Andreas, built by Kiewit Infrastructure West Company.
